newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: "Gene bean" protesters occupy Austrian ministry.
newsitem.headline: "Gene bean" protesters occupy Austrian ministry.

text.p: Activists from the environmental groups Greenpeace and Global 2000 occupied the office of Austrian Health Minister Christa Krammer on Monday to press for an import ban on genetically modified soybeans.

A Greenpeace protester, speaking by telephone from inside Krammer's Vienna office, told Reuters that 30 campaigners had entered the building at 9:30 a.m. and would remain there until the minister responded to their demands.
Krammer was not in her office on Monday morning.
"We will stay here as long as it takes. If the minister does not show today we will consider staying the night," protester Matthias Schickhofer said.

Two demonstrators abseiled down the health ministry, a modern building on the edge of Vienna's historic centre, to unfurl a huge banner bearing the slogan: "Our health is not worth a bean to Frau Krammer. Stop genetically manipulated soya."
Inside, protesters strewed the minister's desk with soybeans and dumped other products containing soya.
Schickhofer said police had so far made no move to eject the activists.
Environmentalists say they fear that the beans, developed by U.S. chemicals giant Monsanto Co to resist the widely used Roundup weedkiller, are unsafe.
Soya is used in some form in a wide range of foodstuffs, including margarine, chocolate and mayonnaise.

The conservative health minister has resisted pressure from environmentalists, shopowners and some government colleagues to slap an import ban on the beans, arguing instead that foods should be clearly labelled so consumers can decide.

Environment Minister Martin Bartenstein has thrown his weight behind the environmentalists' cause. Two leading Austrian supermarket chains, Spar and Julius Meinl, have said they will not stock products containg modified soybeans.
"If Frau Krammer refuses to take our demands on board we will go to the very top. We will involve Chancellor Franz Vranitzky," Schickhofer said.
Genetically altered soybeans from the United States have sparked protests across Europe in recent weeks.
In Germany a Greenpeace barge picketed a ship bearing a cargo of the beans as it sailed up the River Elbe to Hamburg. In Belgium, the group mounted a 24-hour blockade of an Antwerp shipment.
